summary:
No owner lock-out found. I traced every way in on the one address and each still works; the real defects are what the retirement leaves behind on Spark 2, plus one stale generated doc that blocks the lock run.

Ways in, checked against the current code (the suite was not run, and nothing live was touched):
- **Tailscale on the main address:** `requestGate` and `viewerFor` are unchanged apart from the door branches (`service/src/24-handler.mjs:36-47`, `service/src/03-identity.mjs:143`).
- **Passkey from the internet:** `passkeyOrigins()` is now exactly the set the old `mainOrigins()` gave (`service/src/22-passkey.mjs:16`), so every existing passkey still verifies for sign-in and for confirmations (`service/src/22-sessions.mjs:228-250`, `service/src/22-passkey.mjs:171`).
- **Recovery codes:** untouched (`service/src/22-sessions.mjs:252-264`).
- **Terminal sign-in code:** untouched; `tools/console.mjs:22-23` already uses the main address.
- **A fresh device adding its own passkey:** `newDevicePasskeyOpen` and the register route are intact (`service/src/22-sessions.mjs:82`, `service/src/24-handler.mjs:193-211`).
- **Sign-in screen and frame check:** the screen is intact (`public/app.js:5187-5206`); the frame check is now stricter (`public/app.js:5327`) and the service refuses any cross-origin passkey answer (`service/passkey.mjs:97`).
- **whoami, bootstrap, sessions:** only the door and web fields are gone; no removed name is still referenced in the parts or the page, and `server.mjs` matches its parts.
- **Installer:** it changes no route and no Tailscale setting, and still snapshots and rolls back.

Not confirmable from here: whether Spark 2 still has the `spark-console-door` container, `cloud.json`, or a saved invite link. The lens says the container still runs; A1 to A3 assume those leftovers exist.

A4 is outside the access lens but is a confirmed failing check on this tree.

summary:
Security lens, read-only (nothing edited, no SSH, no live console; only `node --check`, `build-server.mjs --check`, `bash -n` and a pure-function snippet were run).

Three real defects, none a lock-out path. Two are guards lost by the removal while the retired pieces are still on Spark 2; one is a hole in the new saved-workflow check.

- **SEC-1 (3):** the short-address device is no longer blocked on the main address, and its removal steps were deleted with nothing replacing them.
- **SEC-2 (2):** the web page's push token (`cloud.json`) now goes into the daily copy on Spark 3, and the test that kept it out was removed.
- **SEC-3 (2):** a saved workflow's input value such as a bare Spark number passes the "said by the owner" check, so Sparkie runs it at once.

Checked and found sound:
- **Removed `req.viaDoor` branches:** every one guarded only the door listener, which is gone (`service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:37-41`). Sessions, agent keys, sign-in, recovery codes, Telegram, hidden files and `/health` behave the same at the main address, through Funnel and from a Spark's address.
- **Passkeys:** with `tops` dropped, an answer from a cross-origin frame is always refused (`service/passkey.mjs:97`), and the origin list is the main address only (`service/src/22-passkey.mjs:16`). The page still shows nothing inside any frame (`public/app.js` `start()`). No stored passkey can be for the short host, so no passkey lock-out.
- **Access requests:** dropping the `web` source only removed its exemption from the per-address limit (`service/src/03-identity.mjs:113`).
- **Owner words:** only the owner's own page chat reaches them (`service/src/24-handler.mjs:615-618`). A near miss only prints `/help`, and what the owner typed is saved as a notice. `restartBrain()` cannot leave `brainRestarting` stuck, because nothing awaits between the busy check and the claim (`service/src/20-heal.mjs:135-140`).
- **Build:** no dangling references to removed functions; `server.mjs` matches its parts; the installer has no leftover variables.

One thing to know before install: the lock names build `aca03d1af018` and the tree is `148b56782a8c`, so the installer will refuse it until `node test/lock.mjs` runs.

findings.title: A saved workflow's input with no word of two letters or more (a bare Spark number) passes the "said by the owner" check
findings.where: service/src/16-actions.mjs:281 (`valuesSaid`); :96 (`tokensOf` drops tokens under 2 characters and generic words); :18-22 (`sparkIdOf` turns "4" into spark4)
findings.fails:
Inputs: a saved workflow "move it" with input `spark` and a step `restart_model {spark: "{spark}", container: "sc-x"}`. The owner types "run move it". The brain, or text it read, calls `run_workflow {name: "move it", inputs: {spark: "4"}}`.

`tokensOf("4")` is empty, and `[].every()` is true, so `valuesSaid` is true. The run starts at once on Spark 4 instead of becoming a button, though the owner never named a Spark. The same happens for the number 4, a one-letter value, or "the model". I confirmed this by running the token rule in isolation.

This is the gap the new check and its test ("input values not in the owner's words … never run at once") were meant to close (R25, R35). Each step's own rails still apply, so Spark 2 stays protected.
findings.fix:
Require at least one token, and name a Spark by its id first:

`const valuesSaid = Object.values(out.inputs || {}).every(v => { const t = [...tokensOf(sparkIdOf(String(v)) || String(v))]; return t.length > 0 && t.every(x => said.has(x)); });`
findings.test: test/steps.test.mjs, in "Sparkie: input values not in the owner's words…": save a workflow with input `spark` used as `"{spark}"`, and script the brain to call `run_workflow` with `inputs: {spark: "4"}` on "run move it". Expect one button, "Run the saved workflow “move it” with spark 4", and no workflow-run operation. "run move it on spark 4" still runs at once.

verdicts.why:
The facts hold, at lower severity (2, not 3), and two parts of the finding do not.

Holds:
- service/src/23-http.mjs:76-80 now blocks only this machine and peers that share a Spark's IPv4. The before snapshot also had `(door && p.DNSName === door)`. Nothing in the current tree reads door.json or names spark-console-door.
- A request from that device's tailnet address passes requestGate (service/src/24-handler.mjs:41-46) and is the owner by Tailscale login, with no session, so the editors open (service/src/22-sessions.mjs:130). Only passkey-gated changes still ask.
- Before, a taken-over door container was held twice: 403 at the main address, and the viaDoor limits on its own socket (no editors, hidden files, sign-in or passkey routes). The socket is closed now, but the main-address block went with it, so the same takeover now reaches the editors' shell.
- The device exists on the real fleet (docs/contract.md:983 retires it; the owner is to remove it by hand). The only removal steps were in deploy/short-address.sh and the "Removing it" section of docs/sharing.md, both deleted. deploy/host-on-portal.sh neither removes it nor mentions it.

Why severity 2: it needs a prior takeover of a small, digest-pinned Tailscale container that only the owner's own tailnet devices can reach (no members or shares existed), and it ends when the owner removes the device. If the owner tagged the device, as the old doc recommended, it carries no login at all; I could not check that.

Does not hold:
- The passkey rows are not a weakened guard. service/passkey.mjs:96 is an exact allowlist, and test/passkey.test.mjs:272-274 and :426-427 still cover another site, the main host without its port, and http.
- The proposed fleet test cannot work as written. Under ALL_LOCAL refreshBlocked never runs (service/src/23-http.mjs:89), the gate uses sparkAddresses() (service/src/24-handler.mjs:41), and test/mock/bin/tailscale answers only `ip`.

`docker rm -f spark-console-door; docker network rm spark-console-door; rm -rf ~/.local/state/spark-console-door ~/.config/spark-console-door ~/.local/share/spark-console-www ~/.local/state/spark-console/door ~/.local/state/spark-console/door.json`

Then the owner deletes the device `sparks` in the Tailscale admin console. The code never touches Tailscale.

2. Keep the block until then, in refreshBlocked (service/src/23-http.mjs:76-79). It stops by itself once door.json is gone:

`const retired = (() => { try { return new URL(readJson(STATE_DIR + '/door.json').origin).hostname + '.'; } catch { return null; } })();`

and add `|| (retired && p.DNSName === retired)` to the peer test at :79.

Do not restore the passkey rows. No stand-in test reaches this guard without a new test switch, which is more machinery than the guard is worth. Check it by review, and after install on Spark 2: door.json gone, no spark-console-door in `docker ps -a`, no `sparks` in `tailscale status`.

summary:
Lens: the round-two fixes. Read-only; nothing was run except `node tools/build-server.mjs --check` (server.mjs matches its parts). The suite was not run.

Seven defects, none a lock-out or a security hole. One is a regression at severity 3, five are gaps the fixes left or opened at severity 2, one is documentation.

- **Regression (3):** the step check now lets every read step pass on a Spark that is off, but five of those reads fail there. A routine can stop a model in step 1 and then fail in step 2, which is what R35 exists to prevent. The new test asserts the wrong result as correct.
- **Gaps (2):**
  - A step with no target is not caught when an earlier step changes the same Spark.
  - One-character input values and names pass the "owner said it" check without being said.
  - "Don't stop anything" from the previous message is ignored for a saved workflow.
  - The near-miss `/help` never fires for a brain that is running but frozen, because its 3-second cap equals the status script's own 3-second curl.
  - `off ||= e` merges an old unpaired offline event with a later dark period.
- **Docs (1):** R19, R35, R25 and the knowledge.json row in architecture.md now say things the code no longer does.

Checked and found sound:
- **`restartBrain`:** the claim on Spark 2 is taken and released in the `finally`. There is no await between the busy check and the claim, so it cannot return null after the owner was told "Restarting", and `watchBrain` marks nothing before a refused restart.
- **Dark Sparks:** the save on a flip, the no-GPU finding and `darkNow` (current dark period only) behave as intended.
- **`changeLabel`:** the button now shows the inputs.
- **Paste card and `/v1`:** the 262,144 ceiling, paste-first ordering and the 429 words are right. `proxyBrain` frees the brain place on every ending.
- **Page `sendWord`:** it does not break the streaming reply or the later refresh. The notice is appended to the same conversation object, the streaming reply stays in the list and keeps drawing, and the saved copy fetched after the stream replaces the list in the server's order.

The status script's curl alone waits 3 s before giving up, plus the docker inspects, so the sleep always wins and `m` is null. It only works when the brain's port refuses at once (stopped, or loading), or when another caller filled the 5-second cache. The stand-in brain reports "not answering" instantly, so no test can see this.

findings.title: `off ||= e` merges an old unpaired spark-offline with a later, real dark period
findings.where: service/src/19-watcher.mjs:89; service/src/16-actions.mjs:524-528 (`darkNow` reads the same list)
findings.fails: events.jsonl holds a spark-offline for Spark 4 with no spark-online after it. Older builds could leave one when the Spark came back around a console restart with knowledge.json still saying online (the review's dark-1 verdict warned of this). A failed knowledge save, or a knowledge.json that was reset, can still leave one. Days later Spark 4 goes dark again: a second spark-offline with its own fresh reading is written, then a spark-online. `off ||= e` keeps the first event, so spark_diagnostics reports one dark period that began days ago, with the old reading and a dark time of days. `restarted` is then judged against that inflated time, so the finding can wrongly read "restarted; it was under GPU load". While it is dark, fleet_status gives the old wentDarkAt and reading. Saving knowledge on a flip stops new duplicates but does nothing for an unpaired event already on disk.
findings.fix: Keep the first offline only when the later one carries no reading, which is what a repeat after a console restart looks like: `if (e.type === 'spark-offline') off = off && !e.last ? off : e;`. A Spark seen going dark live always has a reading under 3 minutes old.
findings.test: test/dark.test.mjs (the second fleet): seed events.jsonl with an old unpaired spark-offline for spark4 (reading A), start with spark4 online, take it offline under a different load and bring it back; expect periods[0].wentDarkAt to equal the new offline's time and lastReading to be the new reading. Today it reports the old time and reading A. The existing restart test (a repeat with last: null keeps the first) must still pass.

So for "run free it" (title tokens [free], intent asked [start]) a call with inputs {where:'4'} is clear and runs at once on a Spark the owner never named, while 'spark4' or 'Spark 4' would have been a button. (with the full stop) still runs at once.

The run_workflow branch looks only at this message's intent.negated and intent.mixed (16-actions.mjs:283) and never at ctx.noStops, so message 2 is clear and runs at once. Its steps run with a fresh ctx (18-workflows.mjs:285) so the stop_model step stops what the owner just said not to stop. The SC-2 fix covered only the same message. Leave the step ctx alone: once this is in, a run that goes at once never has noStops set, and passing it into steps would only make a start step fail mid-run. With a frozen server the curl alone takes the full 3 seconds, so the script always finishes after the 3-second sleep, `m` is null and the function returns null. The text then goes to chatReply (24-handler.mjs:617-619): it is saved as a user turn and waits on the frozen model, with a 300-second idle timeout (14-chats.mjs:269, :304). The fix works only when the port refuses at once (stopped or loading), which is all the test covers (test/words.test.mjs: setBrain('exited')); the stand-in brain fails instantly when hung (test/mock/model.mjs:26-27), so no test can see this.
